chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Dharih al-Muharibi who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Umrah until Hajj (Tamattu') and was prevented after entering the state of Ihram, what should he do? He said: Did he not stipulate to his Lord before entering Ihram that his release from Ihram would be upon any incident that befalls him from Allah's command? I said: Yes, he did stipulate that. He said: Let him return to his family, free (from the obligation of Hajj), there is no sin upon him, for Allah is more deserving to fulfill what was stipulated upon Him. I said: Then is Hajj obligatory upon him next year? He said: No. The meaning in this report is that we interpret it as: if his Hajj is voluntary (Nafl), Hajj is not obligatory upon him next year. But if it is the Hajj of Islam (Fard), then Hajj is necessary next year, according to what the earlier narrations contained.

key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ: Tamattu' (performing Umrah followed by Hajj in the same season)
key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: The obligatory Hajj (the first one required of a Muslim)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone prevented from completing their Hajj after entering Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Istibsar clarifies the ruling for one performing Tamattu' who is prevented (muhsar) after entering Ihram, emphasizing that the condition of 'release upon any obstacle' renders the Hajj null and void, freeing the pilgrim from further obligation. The juristic deduction distinguishes between voluntary Hajj, which does not need to be repeated, and the obligatory Hajj of Islam, which remains binding for the following year. This reflects the Shia principle that stipulations made at the onset of Ihram are binding on God, ensuring fairness in cases of unforeseen impediments.
